title: $(r,s)$-sets from Desarguesian ovoids
summary: An $(r, s)$-${\textit set}$ in ${\rm PG}(n, q)$ is a set of points, say $\mathcal X$, such that each $s$-dimensional projective subspace contains at most $r$ points of $\mathcal X$. We investigate $(n, n-2)$-sets and $(n-2, n-3)$-sets in ${\rm PG}(n, q)$, $n \le 6$. We show that the trivial upper bounds on $(n, n-2)$-sets in ${\rm PG}(n, q)$, $4 \le n \le 6$, $(4, 3)$-sets in ${\rm PG}(6, q)$ and $(3, 2)$-sets in ${\rm PG}(5, q)$ are essentially sharp. A $(3, 2)$-set in ${\rm PG}(13, q)$ of size $\frac{q^6-1}{q-1}$ is also constructed.
